Areas We Cover

Pest control across Eastern Suburbs

Chembur

Older bungalows and societies alongside new redevelopment, close to the refinery and industrial belt at Mahul and Trombay and to the Deonar dumping ground. Waste and industrial land nearby mean steady rodent and fly pressure, and older homes see termites in wooden fittings.

Ghatkopar

Large, long-established societies in Pant Nagar and Garodia Nagar in the east, and the commercial strip along LBS Marg in the west. The older societies benefit most from treating common drains and ducts together, because cockroaches move between flats.

Powai

High-rise complexes such as Hiranandani Gardens, IIT Bombay, offices and a big restaurant scene, all around Powai Lake. The lake and surrounding greenery mean more mosquitoes, and tall buildings need cockroach treatment of shafts and garbage chutes, not just individual kitchens.

Bhandup

Former industrial land now built up with residential towers, sitting between the National Park hills on the west and the Thane Creek mangroves on the east. Expect termites and rodents near the hills and heavy mosquito breeding near the creek during the monsoon.

Mulund

An established residential suburb on the Thane border, with Mulund West close to the forested hills and Mulund East near the creek. Older societies and bungalows see termites and cockroaches; ground floors near open land see rodents.

What drives pest problems in the Eastern Suburbs

The Eastern Suburbs mix old mill and industrial land, fast-growing high-rise complexes and long-established housing societies. Three features shape the pest problems here.

  • Hills and forest on the west: the National Park reaches down to Bhandup and Mulund. Buildings near it see subterranean termites and rodents coming in from open land.
  • Water bodies: Powai Lake, Vihar Lake's catchment and the Thane Creek mangroves all raise mosquito numbers, especially from July to October.
  • Waste and industry: around Chembur, the dumping ground and industrial land support large rat populations, including the lesser bandicoot, a large burrowing rat common in Mumbai.

Rats and the monsoon

Rat urine in floodwater spreads leptospirosis, and Mumbai reports cases every monsoon. If you have seen rats on your premises, act before the rains. We set tamper-resistant bait stations, find and seal entry points, and advise on garbage storage, which does more for the long term than bait alone.

How a treatment works

  1. Inspection. The technician identifies the pest, finds where it is living and how it is getting in, and judges how severe the infestation is.
  2. Treatment plan and quote. You get an itemised quote and a plan: which products, where they go, and whether a follow-up visit is needed.
  3. Treatment. Trained, background-verified technicians carry out the work with WHO and CIB-approved products and tell you about any precautions.
  4. Certificate and follow-up. You receive a treatment certificate after every visit. AMC clients get scheduled follow-up visits and re-treatment at no extra cost between visits.
FAQs

Pest control in Eastern Suburbs: common questions

How much does pest control cost in Powai, Ghatkopar or Mulund?

Prices start at Rs 499 for a cockroach treatment and go up to Rs 3,999 for a comprehensive AMC. We inspect first and then give an itemised quote.

We live in a high-rise in Powai. Why do cockroaches keep coming back?

In tall buildings cockroaches travel through plumbing shafts, ducts and garbage chutes. If only one flat is treated, they come back from the shaft. Treating the shafts and chute rooms, ideally through the society, solves this.

Can you control rats in our society compound?

Yes. We place tamper-resistant bait stations around the perimeter, garbage area and drains, seal gaps where rats enter, and come back to check and refill the stations under an AMC.

Is the treatment safe for children and pets?

We use WHO and CIB-approved products. Bait stations are locked and gel baits sit in cracks out of reach. The technician will advise on any precautions for your home.
